messages.author: ea3b4df809b5f76f
messages.subject: initPackrat fails
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to use packrat with a collaborator — it seems like a really useful tool to avoid dependency hell! However, I'm having great difficulty setting it up. I've pulled his packrat.lock, packrat.sources/, .Rprofile and .Renviron files from Github, and attempted to set up the project to use packrat using initPackrat(), but this fails as follows:

> initPackrat()
Initializing packrat... OK
Installing abind (1.4-0) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing bitops (1.0-6) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing codetools (0.2-8) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing colorspace (1.2-4) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing dichromat (2.0-0) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing digest (0.6.3) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing gtable (0.1.2) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing iterators (1.0.6) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing labeling (0.2) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing lattice (0.20-24) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing MASS (7.3-29) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing plyr (1.8) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing proto (0.3-10) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing RColorBrewer (1.0-5) ... OK (downloaded binary)
Installing RODBC (1.3-9) ... Error: Command failed (1)

This errors kills everything and stops the installation of packages that come alphabetically after RODBC and, if I understand it correctly, fails to initialise packrat at all. Is there a way to troubleshoot this error?

Also, packrat appears to duplicate the packages listed in the 'Packages' panel in RStudio, but doesn't actually load them. Would these duplications be cleared and packages loaded if packrat initialised correctly?

Many thanks for your help, and for this great tool!

Patrick.

messages.author: 5893d17d64b5b0c2
messages.subject: Re: initPackrat fails
parts:
RODBC 1.3-10 is current, so Packrat won't be able to find binaries for 1.3-9 and is likely trying to install RODBC from source, but failing to compile the sources. Trying to build and install manually will probably make the error visible; try this:

1. In packrat.sources/RODBC, you'll find a .tar.gz file with the source for RODBC 1.3-9. Decompress it to a temporary folder.
2. Use devtools::install("/temporary folder/RODBC") to install the package.

In all likelihood this package will fail to build or install with a usable error message. When I tried it on my system I got this:

checking for sqlext.h... no
configure: error: "ODBC headers sql.h and sqlext.h not found"

ERROR: configuration failed for package 'RODBC'
* removing '/private/tmp/Rtmp3f6FLX/Rinsteaad8f342a4/RODBC'
      -----------------------------------
ERROR: package installation failed
Error: Command failed (1)

which suggests that RODBC has some nonstandard build dependencies.

We should probably add something to Packrat to make it possible to see these errors; I opened issue #32 to track this.

For a workaround in your particular scenario, you might try either upgrading to RODBC 1.3-10 (for which binaries are readily available and building is therefore unnecessary) as a temporary fix, or configuring your system such that it's able to build RODBC from source.

Jonathan.

messages.author: bde2181e7d4894f5
messages.subject: Re: initPackrat fails
parts:
I had the same problem, but devtools::install(...) would work just fine.

It seems like the problem is that it is installing from source with dependencies = FALSE, which is understandable since it already downloaded and has the sources for all the dependencies. However, the packages are ordered alphabetically instead of in a dependency order. I solved my the problem by changing packrat.lock and explicitly setting the install order.
